vsm1.6:39.1: (4) He should define it by its direction thus:
vsm1.6:39.2: “There are two directions in this body, that is, down from the navel as the lower direction,
vsm1.6:39.3: and up from it as the upper direction.”
vsm1.6:39.4: Or alternatively, he can define it thus: “I am standing in this direction; the sign of foulness is in that direction.”
vsm1.6:40.1: (5) He should define it by its location thus:
vsm1.6:40.2: “The hand is in this location, the foot in this, the head in this, the middle of the body in this.”
vsm1.6:40.3: Or alternatively, he can define it thus: “I am in this location; the sign of foulness is in that.”
vsm1.6:41.1: (6) He should define it by its delimitation thus:
vsm1.6:41.2: “This body is delimited below by the soles of the feet, above by the tips of the hair, all round by the skin;
vsm1.6:41.3: the space so delimited is filled up with thirty-two pieces of corpse.”
vsm1.6:41.4: Or alternatively, he can define it thus:
vsm1.6:41.5: “This is the delimitation of its hand, this is the delimitation of its foot,
vsm1.6:41.6: this is the delimitation of its head, this is the delimitation of the middle part of its body.”
vsm1.6:41.7: Or alternatively, he can delimit as much of it as he has apprehended thus: “Just this much of the bloated is like this.”
vsm1.6:42.1: However, a female body is not appropriate for a man or a male one for a woman;
vsm1.6:42.2: for the object, namely, the repulsive aspect, does not make its appearance in a body of the opposite sex,
vsm1.6:42.3: which merely becomes a condition for the wrong kind of excitement.
vsm1.6:42.4: To quote the Majjhima Commentary: “Even when decaying, a woman invades a man’s mind and stays there.”
vsm1.6:42.5: That is why the sign should be apprehended in the six ways only in a body of the same sex.
vsm1.6:43.1: But when a clansman has cultivated the meditation subject under former Enlightened Ones, kept the ascetic practices,
vsm1.6:43.2: threshed out the great primary elements, discerned formations, defined mentality-materiality,
vsm1.6:43.3: eliminated the perception of a being, done the ascetic’s duties, lived the moral life, and developed the development,
vsm1.6:43.4: when he contains the seed of turning away from formations, and has mature knowledge and little defilement,
vsm1.6:43.5: then the counterpart sign appears to him in the place while he keeps looking.
vsm1.6:43.6: If it does not appear in that way, then it appears to him as he is apprehending the sign in the six ways.
vsm1.6:44.1: But if it does not appear to him even then,
vsm1.6:44.2:
he should apprehend the sign again in five more ways: (7) by its joints, (8) by its openings,
(9) by its concavities, (10) by its convexities, and (11) all round.
vsm1.6:45.1: Herein, (7) by its joints is properly by its hundred and eighty joints.
vsm1.6:45.2: But how can he define the hundred and eighty joints in the bloated?
vsm1.6:45.3: Consequently he can define it by its fourteen major joints thus: Three joints in the right arm, three in the left arm,
vsm1.6:45.4: three in the right leg, three in the left leg,
vsm1.6:45.5: one neck joint, one waist joint.
vsm1.6:46.2:
an “opening” is the hollow between the arm and the side, the hollow between the legs,
the hollow of the stomach, the hollow of the ear.
vsm1.6:46.3: He should define it by its openings in this way.
vsm1.6:46.4: Or alternatively, the opened or closed state of the eyes and the opened or closed state of the mouth can be defined.
vsm1.6:47.2: he should define any concave place on the body such as the eye sockets or the inside of the mouth or the base of the neck.
vsm1.6:47.3: Or he can define it thus: “I am standing in a concave place, the body is in a convex place.”
vsm1.6:48.1: (10) By its convexities: he should define any raised place on the body such as the knee or the chest or the forehead.
vsm1.6:48.2: Or he can define it thus: “I am standing in a convex place, the body is in a concave place.”
vsm1.6:49.1: (11) All round: the whole body should be defined all round.
vsm1.6:49.2: After working over the whole body with knowledge,
vsm1.6:49.3: he should establish his mind thus, “The bloated, the bloated,” upon any part that appears clearly to him.
vsm1.6:49.4: If it has not appeared even yet,
vsm1.6:49.5: and if there is special intensity of the bloatedness in the belly,
vsm1.6:49.6: he should establish his mind thus, “The bloated, the bloated,” on that.
vsm1.6:50.1: Now, as to the words, he sees that the sign is properly apprehended, etc., the explanation is this.
vsm1.6:50.2: The meditator should apprehend the sign thoroughly in that body in the way of apprehending the sign already described.
vsm1.6:50.3: He should advert to it with well-established mindfulness.
vsm1.6:50.4: He should see that it is properly remembered, properly defined, by doing that again and again.
vsm1.6:50.5: Standing in a place not too far from and not too near to the body, he should open his eyes, look and apprehend the sign.
vsm1.6:50.6:
He should open his eyes and look a hundred times, a thousand times, thinking,
“Repulsiveness of the bloated, repulsiveness of the bloated,”
vsm1.6:50.7: and he should close his eyes and advert to it.
vsm1.6:51.1: As he does so again and again, the learning sign becomes properly apprehended by him.
vsm1.6:51.3: When it comes into focus alike whether he opens his eyes and looks or closes his eyes and adverts,
vsm1.6:51.4: then it is called properly apprehended.
vsm1.6:52.1: When he has thus properly apprehended the sign, properly remembered it, and properly defined it,
vsm1.6:52.2: then if he is unable to conclude his development on the spot,
vsm1.6:52.3: he can go to his own lodging, alone, in the same way as described of his coming, with no companion,
vsm1.6:52.4: keeping that same meditation subject in mind, with mindfulness well established,
vsm1.6:52.5: and with his mind not turned outwards owing to his faculties being turned inwards.
vsm1.6:53.1: As he leaves the charnel ground he should define the path he comes back by thus:
vsm1.6:53.2: “The path by which I have left goes in an easterly direction, westerly … northerly … southerly direction,”
vsm1.6:53.3: or “It goes in an intermediate direction”;
vsm1.6:53.4: or “In this place it goes to the left, in this place to the right”;
vsm1.6:53.5: and “In this place there is a stone, in this a termite-mound, in this a tree, in this a bush, in this a creeper.”
vsm1.6:54.1: When he has defined the path he has come back by
vsm1.6:54.2: and when, once back, he is walking up and down, he should see that his walk is oriented towards it too;
vsm1.6:54.3: the meaning is that he should walk up and down on a piece of ground that faces in the direction of the sign of foulness.
vsm1.6:54.4: And when he sits, he should prepare a seat oriented towards it too.
vsm1.6:55.1: But if there is a bog or a ravine or a tree or a fence or a swamp in that direction,
vsm1.6:55.2: if he cannot walk up and down on a piece of ground facing in that direction,
vsm1.6:55.3: if he cannot prepare his seat thus because there is no room for it,
vsm1.6:55.4: then he can both walk up and down and sit in a place where there is room, even though it does not face that way;
vsm1.6:55.5: but he should turn his mind in that direction.
vsm1.6:56.1: Now, as to the questions beginning with what is the purpose … characterizing the surrounding signs?
vsm1.6:56.2: The intention of the answer that begins with the words, has non-delusion for its purpose, is this:
vsm1.6:56.3: If someone goes at the wrong time to the place where the sign of the bloated is,
vsm1.6:56.4: and opens his eyes for the purpose of apprehending the sign by characterizing the surrounding signs,
vsm1.6:56.5: then as soon as he looks the dead body appears as if it were standing up
vsm1.6:56.7: and when he sees the hideous and fearful object,
vsm1.6:56.8: his mind reels, he is like one demented,
vsm1.6:56.9: gripped by panic, fear and terror, and his hair stands on end.
vsm1.6:56.10: For among the thirty-eight meditation subjects expounded in the texts no object is so frightening as this one.
vsm1.6:56.11: There are some who lose jhāna in this meditation subject.
vsm1.6:57.1: So the meditator must stand firm.
vsm1.6:57.2: Establishing his mindfulness well, he should remove his fears in this way:
vsm1.6:57.3: “No dead body gets up and pursues one.
vsm1.6:57.4: If that stone or that creeper close to it were to come, the body might come too;
vsm1.6:57.5: but since that stone or that creeper does not come, the body will not come either.
vsm1.6:57.6: Its appearance to you in this way is born: of your perception, created by your perception.
vsm1.6:57.7: Today your meditation subject has appeared to you.
vsm1.6:57.9: He should laugh it off and direct his mind to the sign.
vsm1.6:57.10: In that way he will arrive at distinction.
vsm1.6:57.11: The words “Characterizing the surrounding signs has non-delusion for its purpose” are said on this account.
vsm1.6:58.1: To succeed in apprehending the sign in the eleven ways is to anchor the meditation subject.
vsm1.6:58.2: For the opening of his eyes and looking conditions the arising of the learning sign;
vsm1.6:58.3: and as he exercises his mind on that the counterpart sign arises;
vsm1.6:58.4: and as he exercises his mind on that he reaches absorption.
vsm1.6:58.5: When he is sure of absorption, he works up insight and realizes Arahantship.
vsm1.6:58.6: Hence it was said: apprehending the sign in the other eleven ways has anchoring the mind for its purpose.
vsm1.6:59.1: The reviewing of the path gone by and come by has keeping the mind on the track for its purpose:
vsm1.6:59.2: the meaning is that the reviewing of the path gone by and of the path come back by mentioned
vsm1.6:59.3: is for the purpose of keeping properly to the track of the meditation subject.
vsm1.6:60.1: For if this bhikkhu is going along with his meditation subject and people on the way
vsm1.6:60.2: ask him about the day, “What is today, venerable sir?”
vsm1.6:60.3: or they ask him some question about Dhamma,
vsm1.6:60.5: he ought not to go on in silence, thinking “I have a meditation subject.”
vsm1.6:60.6: The day must be told, the question must be answered,
vsm1.6:60.7: even by saying “I do not know” if he does not know,
vsm1.6:60.8: a legitimate welcome must be responded to.
vsm1.6:60.9: As he does so, the newly acquired sign vanishes.
vsm1.6:60.10: But even if it does vanish, he should still tell the day when asked;
vsm1.6:60.11: if he does not know the answer to the question, he should still say “I do not know,”
vsm1.6:60.12: and if he does know it, he should explain it surely; and he must respond to a welcome.
vsm1.6:60.13: Also reception of visitors must be attended to on seeing a visiting bhikkhu,
vsm1.6:60.14:
and all the remaining duties in the Khandhakas must be carried out too, that is, the duties of the shrine terrace,
the duties of the Bodhi-tree terrace, the duties of the Uposatha house, the duties of the refectory and the bath
house, and those to the teacher, the preceptor, visitors, departing bhikkhus, and the rest.
vsm1.6:61.1: And the newly acquired sign vanishes while he is carrying out these too.
vsm1.6:61.2: When he wants to go again, thinking “I shall go and take up the sign,”
vsm1.6:61.3: he finds he cannot go to the charnel ground because it has been invaded by non-human beings or by wild beasts,
vsm1.6:61.5: For a bloated corpse only lasts one or two days and then turns into a livid corpse.
vsm1.6:61.6: Of all the meditation subjects there is none so hard to come by as this.
vsm1.6:62.1: So when the sign has vanished in this way,
vsm1.6:62.2: the bhikkhu should sit down in his night quarters or in his day quarters
vsm1.6:62.3:
and first of all review the path gone by and come by up to the place where he
is actually sitting cross-legged, doing it in this way:
vsm1.6:62.4: “I went out of the monastery by this gate,
vsm1.6:62.5: I took a path leading in such and such a direction,
vsm1.6:62.6: I turned left at such and such a place,
vsm1.6:62.7: I turned right at such and such a place,
vsm1.6:62.8: in one part of it there was a stone, in another a termite-mound or a tree or a bush or a creeper;
vsm1.6:62.9: having gone by that path, I saw the foulness in such and such a place,
vsm1.6:62.10: I stood there facing in such and such a direction
vsm1.6:62.11: and observed such and such surrounding signs,
vsm1.6:62.12: I apprehended the sign of foulness in this way;
vsm1.6:62.13: I left the charnel ground in such and such a direction,
vsm1.6:62.14: I came back by such and such a path doing this and this,
vsm1.6:62.15: and I am now sitting here.”
vsm1.6:63.1: As he reviews it in this way, the sign becomes evident and appears as if placed in front of him;
vsm1.6:63.2: the meditation subject rides in its track as it did before.
vsm1.6:63.3: Hence it was said: the reviewing of the path gone by and come by has keeping the mind on the track for its purpose.
vsm1.6:64.1:
Now, as to the words, when he has established reverence for it by seeing its advantages and by perceiving
it as a treasure and so come to love it, he anchors the mind on that object:
vsm1.6:64.2: here, having gained jhāna by exercising his mind on the repulsiveness in the bloated,
vsm1.6:64.3: he should increase insight with the jhāna as its proximate cause,
vsm1.6:64.4: and then he should see the advantages in this way: “Surely in this way I shall be liberated from ageing and death.”
vsm1.6:65.1: Just as a pauper who acquired a treasure of gems
vsm1.6:65.2:
would guard and love it with great affection, feeling reverence for it as one who appreciates
the value of it, “I have got what is hard indeed to get!”
vsm1.6:65.3: so too this bhikkhu should guard the sign, loving it and feeling reverence for it as one who appreciates the value of it,
vsm1.6:65.4: “I have got this meditation subject, which is indeed as hard to get as a very valuable treasure is for a pauper to get.
vsm1.6:65.5: For one whose meditation subject is the four elements discerns the four primary elements in himself,
vsm1.6:65.6: one whose meditation subject is breathing discerns the wind in his own nostrils,
vsm1.6:65.7: and one whose meditation subject is a kasiṇa makes a kasiṇa and develops it at his ease,
vsm1.6:65.8: so these other meditation subjects are easily got.
vsm1.6:65.9: But this one lasts only one, or two days, after which it turns into a livid corpse.
vsm1.6:65.10: There is none harder to get than this one.”
vsm1.6:65.11: In his night quarters and in his day quarters
vsm1.6:65.12: he should keep his mind anchored there thus, “Repulsiveness of the bloated, repulsiveness of the bloated.”
vsm1.6:65.13: And he should advert to the sign, bring it to mind and strike at it with thought and applied thought over and over again.
vsm1.6:66.1: As he does so, the counterpart sign arises.
vsm1.6:66.2: Here is the difference between the two signs.
vsm1.6:66.3: The learning sign appears as a hideous, dreadful and frightening sight;
vsm1.6:66.4: but the counterpart sign appears like a man with big limbs lying down after eating his fill.
vsm1.6:67.1: Simultaneously with his acquiring the counterpart sign,
vsm1.6:67.2: his lust is abandoned by suppression owing to his giving no attention externally to sense desires as object.
vsm1.6:67.3: And owing to his abandoning of approval, ill will is abandoned too, as pus is with the abandoning of blood.
vsm1.6:67.4: Likewise stiffness and torpor are abandoned through exertion of energy,
vsm1.6:67.5: agitation and worry are abandoned through devotion to peaceful things that cause no remorse;
vsm1.6:67.6:
and uncertainty about the Master who teaches the way, about the way, and about the fruit of the way,
is abandoned through the actual experience of the distinction attained.
vsm1.6:67.7: So the five hindrances are abandoned.
vsm1.6:67.8: And there are present applied thought with the characteristic of directing the mind on to that same sign,
vsm1.6:67.9: and sustained thought accomplishing the function of pressing on the sign,
vsm1.6:67.10: and happiness due to the acquisition of distinction,
vsm1.6:67.11: and tranquillity due to the production of tranquillity in one whose mind is happy,
vsm1.6:67.12: and bliss with that tranquillity as its sign,
vsm1.6:67.13: and unification that has bliss as its sign due to the production of concentration in one whose mind is blissful.
vsm1.6:67.14: So the jhāna factors become manifest.
vsm1.6:68.1: Thus access, which is the obverse of the first jhāna, is produced in him too at that same moment.
vsm1.6:68.2: All after that up to absorption in the first jhāna and mastery in it should be understood as described under the earth kasiṇa.
vsm1.6:69.1: As regards the livid and the rest:
vsm1.6:69.2:
the characterizing already described, starting with the going in the way beginning “One who is learning the bloated
sign of foulness goes alone with no companion, with unremitting mindfulness established” (§19),
vsm1.6:69.3:
should all be understood with its exposition and intention, substituting for the word “bloated” the appropriate word in each
case thus: “One who is learning the livid sign of foulness …”, “One who is learning the festering sign of foulness …”
vsm1.6:69.4: But the differences are as follows.
